$comment: Task-skill catalog — verified agent-skill records for common task domains. Each entry carries the full verification rubric: skill exists (source recorded), trigger boundaries, reproducible fixture, baseline comparison, failure modes, permissions, prerequisites. evalStatus: verified (inspected + documented) | fixture-pending (exists, fixture defined, run not yet published). Honest statuses only — a fixture-pending entry is not an evaluation.

entries.trigger: When a UI needs structured critique — visual hierarchy, copy, interaction gaps — before or instead of a redesign.
entries.notFor: Pure layout bugs (fix the bug, don't critique it); brand-new greenfield design (use frontend-design instead).
entries.fixture: Run the skill on a fixed screenshot/DOM capture of a real page; compare its issue list against a human-written critique of the same capture.
entries.baseline: Without the skill, an agent's critique is generic ('improve contrast') — the skill enforces a systematic pass across hierarchy, copy, states.
failureModes: Over-critique: redesigns more than asked
Misses domain-specific conventions the skill wasn't trained on
prereqs: a screenshot, DOM, or running page to critique

entries.trigger: Greenfield visual direction — new page, new section, new design language — where exploration is the point.
entries.notFor: Bug fixes, refactors, or matching an existing design system exactly (that's minimal-change work).
entries.fixture: Give the same design brief to the skill and to a vanilla agent; diff the two prototypes on coherence, reusability, and constraint-following.
entries.baseline: Vanilla agents produce generic landing-page styling; the design skill pushes systematic token/component thinking.
failureModes: Invents a design system conflicting with the existing one
Browser verification skipped → visual bugs shipped
entries.permissions: writes new frontend code; browser preview for verification
prereqs: a repo or sandbox to build in

entries.trigger: Auditing an interface against WCAG — keyboard paths, screen-reader output, contrast, focus management.
entries.notFor: Writing new components (audit after building); automated-axe-only passes (the skill exists because tooling alone misses real usage).
entries.fixture: Run against a page with seeded violations (missing labels, broken focus order, low contrast); measure detection rate against the seed list.
entries.baseline: Without it, agents run automated checks and declare victory — the skill's default is 'untested until a screen reader says otherwise.'
failureModes: Reports issues it can't verify without assistive tech access
Severity ratings can drift without a rubric
entries.permissions: read-only audit; may drive a browser

entries.trigger: Diagnosing real load performance — LCP, CLS, render-blocking, network waterfalls — on a running page.
entries.notFor: Theoretical optimization without measurement; bundle-size-only concerns (a bundle analyzer fits better).
entries.fixture: Trace a known-slow page; compare the skill's bottleneck diagnosis against the waterfall evidence.
entries.baseline: Without DevTools access, agents guess at causes ('optimize images') — the skill forces evidence-first diagnosis.
failureModes: Fixes the metric not the cause (lazy-loading the LCP element makes it worse)
Lab-vs-field divergence ignored
prereqs: running page (local or staging preferred over prod)

entries.trigger: Driving a real logged-in browser — form flows, checkout tests, pixel/GTM checks, logged-in-only errors, hosting-panel logs.
entries.notFor: Headless CI scraping (use Playwright directly); sites forbidding automation.
entries.fixture: Complete a fixed multi-step flow (login → form → verify state) in the user's real browser; assert the end state.
entries.baseline: Without it, agents write Playwright scripts that fail on auth/SSO walls the real browser already clears.
failureModes: Acts in the user's real session — irreversible actions need explicit confirmation
Selector fragility on dynamic SPAs
entries.permissions: full control of the user's real Chrome session — highest-trust tool

entries.source: skill: motion (motion/react, motion-v); MCP: motion codex
entries.trigger: Any animation work — Motion/Framer Motion code, CSS springs, transition tuning, jank audits.
entries.notFor: Static layouts; teams not using Motion (skill is Motion-first but covers CSS springs).
entries.fixture: Implement a fixed transition spec (spring curve, duration budget); audit with MotionScore for layout thrash.
entries.baseline: Without it, agents write linear() easings by feel and import framer-motion — the skill enforces current Motion APIs and performance budgets.
failureModes: Reduced-motion preference ignored unless checked
Animating layout properties instead of transform/opacity
prereqs: reduced-motion check in the acceptance criteria

entries.trigger: Multi-source investigation where the answer must cite sources — market scans, technology evaluations, literature reviews.
entries.notFor: Single-fact lookups (just fetch the page); questions answerable from the codebase (use subagent_explore).
entries.fixture: Ask a question with a known correct answer from primary sources; check the report cites those sources, not SEO aggregators.
entries.baseline: Vanilla web-search agents cite listicles; the skill enforces source-first (primary docs, papers, official records) research.
failureModes: Confident synthesis over thin sources
Source-count inflation (30 citations ≠ 30 independent sources)
prereqs: a researchable question with verifiable ground truth

entries.trigger: Technical SEO audits, content-intent mapping, internal-link structure, organic-growth strategy.
entries.notFor: Keyword-stuffing exercises or thin-page generation (the site's own rule: coverage earns traffic, not the reverse).
entries.fixture: Audit a fixed site section; compare the skill's issue list against a manual crawl (titles, canonicals, internal links, schema).
entries.baseline: Without it, SEO advice degenerates to meta-tag checklists — the skill works at strategy level (intent mapping, link authority).
failureModes: Recommends volume over usefulness — the failure this site's checklist exists to prevent
Tactics that age badly (scaled thin pages)

entries.trigger: Auditing whether AI engines (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity) cite a brand — and why competitors get cited instead.
entries.notFor: Fan-out spam to game citations (explicitly out of bounds); classic rank tracking (that's seo-specialist).
entries.fixture: Query a fixed prompt set across AI engines; log citation presence/absence and the cited sources for diffing over time.
entries.baseline: Without it, 'do AI engines mention us' is anecdote — the skill structures the audit (prompt fixtures, citation logging, competitor diff).
failureModes: AI-engine answers are stochastic — single-run conclusions mislead
Conflates mention with accurate recommendation

entries.trigger: Developer docs, API references, READMEs, tutorials — turning engineering concepts into docs developers read.
entries.notFor: Marketing copy, changelogs that should be generated, or docs nobody will maintain.
entries.fixture: Give the same feature spec; compare the skill's doc structure (task-oriented, runnable examples) against a vanilla writeup.
entries.baseline: Vanilla agents write walls of exposition — the skill produces task-first structure with tested examples.
failureModes: Docs drift from code truth (the skill can't fix an unmaintained doc)
Over-structuring trivial features
prereqs: access to the actual code/feature being documented

entries.trigger: Creating or editing .docx deliverables — reports, proposals — where the output must be a real Word file.
entries.notFor: Markdown-native content (don't convert to docx without need); documents that should be web pages.
entries.fixture: Generate a styled .docx from a fixed brief; open it (render verification) and check styles/structure survive.
entries.baseline: Without a doc skill, agents emit Markdown and call it a document — the skill produces actual Word artifacts with render QA.
failureModes: Renders fine in the editor, broken in Word/LibreOffice (always render-check)
Style drift from template
prereqs: render/QA loop on the produced file

entries.trigger: Extracting data from PDFs (tables, forms, scans) or producing PDFs that must render correctly.
entries.notFor: HTML pages that should stay HTML; PDFs a simple text dump handles.
entries.fixture: Extract a fixed table from a known PDF; verify cell-by-cell accuracy; create a PDF and render-check page 1.
entries.baseline: Vanilla agents regex text dumps and lose table structure — the skill uses proper extraction paths and rendered QA.
failureModes: Scanned PDFs need OCR path — text extraction returns garbage
Complex layouts scramble reading order

entries.trigger: Creating slide decks where the deliverable is a real .pptx or rendered deck.
entries.notFor: Speaker notes only (write the doc); decks that should be one-pagers.
entries.fixture: Produce a deck from a fixed outline; render slides and check layout/overflow visually.
entries.baseline: Vanilla output is bullet-walls in a file — the skill handles layout, visual hierarchy, and render QA.
failureModes: Text overflow past slide bounds (render-check mandatory)
Bullet-heavy when a diagram was needed

entries.trigger: Live spreadsheet work — reading/editing open Calc files, formulas, charts, recalculation.
entries.notFor: CSV-only data (scripts are simpler); Excel files needing Excel-specific features.
entries.fixture: Open a fixed .ods, read a formula, write a computed column, recalculate, verify the values — all through the live bridge.
entries.baseline: Without it, agents parse files statically and can't see formula results — the UNO bridge works on the live document.
failureModes: Formula locales differ (functions named differently)
Recalculation assumptions silently wrong

entries.source: agent environment; LMVersity AGENTS.md rules 1-11 constrain usage
entries.trigger: Decorative/mood imagery only — never anything asserting a fact (no diagrams, charts, text, people).
entries.notFor: Factual diagrams (hand-authored SVG only), any embedded text, anything mistakable for data — the site rules are absolute.
entries.fixture: Generate against the rules checklist: light ground, two-brand-colors, flat vector, no text, square — then verify the output obeys.
entries.baseline: Unconstrained generation produces invented-diagram and pseudo-text artifacts — the rules exist because those are editorial violations.
failureModes: Hallucinated text in-image
Photorealistic output against a flat-vector brand
Generated 'data' that implies a false claim
entries.permissions: generates image files; no shell commands during generation

entries.trigger: Analysis over real datasets where formulas/computations must check out — not narrative summaries of data.
entries.notFor: Data the agent should just read (don't compute what's already computed); datasets too large for the tools.
entries.fixture: Compute a known statistic from a fixed dataset two ways (formula + script); require agreement before reporting.
entries.baseline: Vanilla agents narrate plausible numbers — the skill forces computed values with source+formula provenance.
failureModes: Silent formula errors (verify by recomputation)
Sample-vs-population confusion in reported stats

entries.trigger: Reviewing a diff/PR for correctness, security, maintainability, performance — constructive, actionable feedback.
entries.notFor: Style-preference nitpicking, rubber-stamping, or reviewing code you can't see fully.
entries.fixture: Review a PR with seeded bugs (off-by-one, injection, race); measure catch rate and false-positive rate.
entries.baseline: Vanilla reviews praise-then-nitpick — the skill defaults to finding real correctness/security issues first.
failureModes: Misses context outside the diff (needs repo access, not just the patch)
Severity inflation on style issues
prereqs: the diff plus enough surrounding context

entries.trigger: Bug fixes where the diff must stay small — three similar lines beat a premature abstraction.
entries.notFor: Refactors, features, or anything where scope creep is actually warranted.
entries.fixture: Give a bug + sprawling codebase; measure diff size and whether the fix addressed only the reported bug.
entries.baseline: Vanilla agents refactor surrounding code 'while in there' — the skill's discipline is the minimum viable diff.
failureModes: Too minimal: papers over a structural bug that needs more than a local fix
Ignores adjacent identical bugs

entries.trigger: Turning vague instructions into reliable LLM behaviors — systematic prompt crafting with fixtures and evals.
entries.notFor: One-off prompts you'll never reuse (just write it); problems needing fine-tuning not prompting.
entries.fixture: Build a prompt against a fixed test set; run the eval matrix; iterate on failures, not vibes.
entries.baseline: Vanilla prompt edits are anecdote-driven ('seemed better') — the skill demands fixtures and measured eval.
failureModes: Overfits the fixture (hold out a set)
Prompt patches that mask model-capability limits

entries.trigger: Turning scattered sources into a weighted evidence map — what the evidence actually supports vs what's claimed.
entries.notFor: Single-source summaries; debates where you already know the answer you want.
entries.fixture: Feed a mixed-quality source pile on a known question; check the synthesis weights primary evidence over commentary.
entries.baseline: Vanilla synthesis averages sources democratically — the skill weights by evidence quality and flags uncertainty.
failureModes: False balance between strong and weak evidence
Uncertainty markers dropped in summary
prereqs: the source pile or a research question

entries.trigger: Quantitative claims — experiment design, significance, separating signal from noise and bias.
entries.notFor: Arithmetic; descriptive stats where inference isn't needed.
entries.fixture: Present a study design with a known flaw (underpowered, selection bias, p-hacked); check detection.
entries.baseline: Vanilla agents accept significance claims at face value — the skill pressure-tests design before claims.
failureModes: Confidence beyond what the design supports
Methodology critique that misses the practical question
prereqs: the data, design, or claim under test

entries.trigger: Provider-specific deployment — Foundry agents end-to-end, or environment.yaml snapshot-setup for repos.
entries.notFor: General Azure/cloud deploys outside Foundry scope; deployments without a rollback story.
entries.fixture: Dry-run a deployment on a test target; verify the rollback path is exercised, not just documented.
entries.baseline: Vanilla deploys are imperative and unrepeatable — the skills encode the provider's actual workflow.
failureModes: Permission boundaries crossed silently (deploys are privileged)
Rollback path assumed, never tested

entries.trigger: Installing, configuring, or auditing plugins/connectors/MCP servers — permissions, dependencies, data access.
entries.notFor: Writing plugins (that's build work); first-party config the plugin system doesn't touch.
entries.fixture: Audit a fixed plugin set: enumerate requested permissions vs declared need; flag over-broad access.
entries.baseline: Vanilla installs click through permission prompts — the skill makes permission/data-access review the gate.
failureModes: Supply-chain risk in third-party connectors
Permission creep after updates re-requests scopes
entries.permissions: modifies the agent's own capabilities — review-tier
